financing.summary: Mattamy Homes U.S. does not borrow on its own. It is funded centrally by its Canadian parent, Mattamy Group Corporation (owned through Mattamy Asset Management, the Gilgan family holding company), which issues Rule 144A/Reg S senior unsecured notes in US$ and C$ and runs one cross-border bank revolver that funds both countries. In December 2025 the group sold US$475M of 6.00% notes due 2033 and C$350M of new notes. It used the proceeds to retire its US$500M 5.25% notes due 2027 and C$250M 4.625% notes due 2028 and to pay down the revolver. That leaves no bond maturity before the US$ 4.625% notes due March 2030. The bank line is a three-year, $2.1B sustainability-linked revolver set up in fall 2024, so its renewal (about fall 2027) is the next big refinancing date. Mattamy is a land developer as much as a builder: it is master developer and majority landowner at Wellen Park (Venice, FL) and develops Tradition (Port St. Lucie, FL). Its 2025-2026 US land releases describe outright closings, either raw land or finished lots bought from master developers, and none mentions a land banker or option partner. That makes Mattamy an under-penetrated prospect for land banking, not an existing land-bank user. Owned-versus-optioned lot data is not public: financial statements go only to certified noteholders through Intralinks.
financing.land_strategy: Owns most / developer model, inferred from the company's own releases. Mattamy calls itself master developer and majority landowner at Wellen Park (22,500 homes at build-out) and develops Tradition (Port St. Lucie). Its 2025-2026 US land announcements are outright purchases. Examples: 76 acres in Fort Mill, SC for $13M (193 homes); 65 and 29 acres near Charlotte (187 + 61 homes); 70 finished lots in Avondale, AZ for $6.37M; 145 lots at Verona (Pasco County, FL), a master plan led by Eisenhower Property Group; 154 lots at Twin Peaks Crossings (Marana, AZ); and 59 and 71 finished lots in Glendale and Tucson, AZ (both closed 2026-10-29). Mattamy publishes no optioned-lot target and has never disclosed a land-light goal.

lots.source_title: Mattamy Group Corporation Announces First Quarter 2027 Key Operating Results (2026-10-20)
lots.note: Lot counts are not publicly disclosed. The quarterly releases give only revenue, closings, net orders and backlog, and full financial statements are posted on Intralinks for certified noteholders and prospective QIBs only (we did not request access). Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended 2026-08-31), group-wide US + Canada: revenue 1.02B (currency not stated in the release), 1,465 closings, 1,905 net orders (+24%), backlog 3,587 units. FY2026 (year ended 2026-05-31): revenue 5.90B (-7.9%), 8,261 closings, 7,474 net orders.

land_banking.description: Master developer of Verona, a 2,500-home multi-builder master plan in Land O' Lakes (Pasco County, FL). Mattamy bought 145 lots there (73 40-ft and 72 50-ft), closing on 2026-06-05, with sales starting in summer 2027. This is a lot purchase from a developer, not option or land-bank financing. It is listed here because it shows how Mattamy sources finished lots.
land_banking.source_title: Mattamy Homes Expands Tampa Presence with Land Acquisition in Pasco County (2026-06-29)
land_banking.note: Price not disclosed. Verifier 2026-11-19: the release names Eisenhower Property Group as Verona's master developer but does not name the seller of the 145 lots, so Eisenhower as the counterparty is inferred.

debt.lenders_agent: Syndicate of Canadian and US banks; agent and lenders not named
debt.note: Mattamy renewed and amended its existing revolver in fall 2024 into a three-year, $2.1B sustainability-linked facility that gives cross-border working capital. It calls this the first sustainability-linked revolver for a North American homebuilder. The report does not say whether $2.1B is C$ or US$, so principal_usd_m is null. A three-year term from fall 2024 implies maturity around fall 2027 (inferred, not stated). The Dec-2025 notes repaid part of the revolver borrowings, so drawn amounts exist, but they are not public.

capital_events.description: Completed a two-tranche 144A/Reg S senior unsecured offering: US$475M (6.00% due 2033 per Cbonds) and C$350M. Proceeds go to redeem the US$500M 5.25% notes due 2027 and the C$250M 4.625% notes due 2028, to repay revolver borrowings and to pay fees.
capital_events.source_title: Mattamy Group Corporation Announces Completion of its US$475 Million and CAD$350 Million Senior Unsecured Notes Offering
capital_events.note: amount_usd_m counts the US$ tranche only; the C$350M tranche is extra. Cravath represented the initial purchasers (https://www.cravath.com/news-insights/mattamy-group-corporations-highyield-senior-notes-offerings.html).

capital_events.description: Full redemption of the US$500M 5.250% senior notes due 2027 and the C$250M 4.625% senior notes due 2028, funded by the Dec-2025 offering. This pushed the group's nearest bond maturity out to March 2030.
capital_events.source_title: Mattamy Group Corporation Announces Completion of its US$475 Million and CAD$350 Million Senior Unsecured Notes Offering
capital_events.note: Stated as intended use of proceeds; the exact redemption date was not seen. amount_usd_m excludes the C$250M series.

capital_events.description: Renewed and amended the group's bank revolver into a three-year, $2.1B sustainability-linked revolving loan with a syndicate of Canadian and US banks. Pricing is tied to GHG-emissions and energy-intensity KPIs.
capital_events.note: The report says only 'fall 2024'; the month is approximate. Currency of the $2.1B is not stated. This is context from before 2025.

capital_events.description: Parent Mattamy Asset Management appointed Eric Becker (founder and co-chairman of Cresset, a multi-family office; co-founder of private-equity firm Sterling Partners) to its board. The board is chaired by Kathleen Taylor (former RBC chair), who has been chair since May 2025.
capital_events.source_title: Mattamy Asset Management Appoints Eric Becker to its Board of Directors
capital_events.note: Governance context for the parent that funds the US business; it is not a capital transaction.

joint_ventures.description: Co-development of a 253-acre master plan south of Chestermere Lake, Alberta, with about 1,900 homes. Mattamy's Alberta Division is managing partner, and the deal closed on 2026-01-20. This is a Canadian JV, not US, and is recorded because it shows how the parent partners on land.
joint_ventures.source_title: Mattamy Homes and Truman partner on new 253-acre community in Chestermere, AB (2026-02-02)
joint_ventures.note: No US JVs found in 2025-2026 releases.

key_metrics.credit_ratings: S&P: BB+ / stable (upgraded from BB in late 2023, per a secondary report that cites S&P's then-metrics of debt/EBITDA under 2x and EBITDA interest cover of 10-11x). Moody's: Ba1 corporate family rating (upgraded from Ba2), with senior unsecured notes at Ba2. The Moody's action was seen only in a search-result title and its date was not confirmed. Neither rating was checked on the agency's own site.
key_metrics.source_title: BriefGlance: Mattamy Homes Secures $825M in Strategic Debt Overhaul (Dec 2025)

gaps: Owned vs optioned lots, total lots controlled and years of supply: not publicly disclosed. Mattamy's financial statements go only to certified noteholders and prospective QIBs through Intralinks, and we did not request access because that requires certifying identity on a form.
US-only financials (revenue, debt, inventory): not publicly disclosed. Releases report US + Canada combined, and the currency is not stated in the releases.
Total debt, cash, liquidity, net debt to capital: not publicly disclosed (Intralinks only).
Coupon and maturity of the C$350M December 2025 notes: not found in public sources (the company release and the Cravath deal note omit them, and no Cbonds page was located).

Revolver: currency of the $2.1B, exact maturity, administrative agent, lender list and drawn balance are not publicly disclosed. The sustainability report names only 'a syndicate of Canadian and American financial institutions'.
Amount still outstanding on the 4.625% US$ notes due 2030 (US$600M issued per Cbonds): not confirmed, because any partial repurchases are not public.
Mortgage-subsidiary (Mattamy Home Funding) warehouse lines: not publicly disclosed.

Land-banking or lot-option counterparties (Millrose, Kennedy Lewis, TPG Angelo Gordon, Domain, Varde, Essential Housing, IHP, Brookfield, Oaktree, GTIS, Hearthstone, Walton, Forestar): none found. No Mattamy press release in 2025-2026 mentions an option or land-bank partner, a search of Domain's and IHP's own sites returned nothing on Mattamy, and Varde's and Millrose's sites blocked automated access.

M&A: no builder acquisitions, divestitures or mergers involving Mattamy Homes U.S. found for 2025 to 2026-11-19, either in the company newsroom (all releases reviewed) or in a targeted search. Land and lot purchases are recorded under land_strategy, not as M&A.
Credit ratings: not confirmed on the S&P, Moody's or DBRS Morningstar sites (paywalled or bot-blocked). Current outlooks and any rating on the Dec-2025 notes are not confirmed.
